newsitem.title: UAE: Air freight seen outpacing passenger traffic rise.
newsitem.headline: Air freight seen outpacing passenger traffic rise.

text.p: Air freight growth will outpace passenger air traffic growth in all major markets for the next 20 years, Boeing's regional director marketing-cargo said on Sunday.
"Average annual freight traffic growth is expected to reach 6.7 percent from 1995 to 2015 while passenger traffic growth will be around 5.1 percent a year," said David Pierce, a noted forecaster.
Pierce was speaking at a two-day air cargo conference in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

The growth in air freight versus passenger traffic was particularly noticable on trans-Atlantic routes, where cargo growth was estimated at 7.0 percent per annum from 1995 to 2015 against 4.1 percent for passengers, he said.

In southeast Asia annual air freight growth was seen rising by 9.0 percent versus 6.7 percent for passengers and in North America freight was seen increasing by 5.5 percent a year against 3.6 percent for passengers.

The growth discrepencies were evident across the globe, he said, but less dramatic in other areas. In Europe the figures were 4.5 percent growth against 4.0 percent and in Asia 7.4 percent versus 6.7 percent.
On Pacific routes annual cargo growth of 8.0 percent compared with 6.6 percent for passenger traffic, he said.
The air cargo conference, which began on Sunday, is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a global organisation for airports.
